outcome: Database provisioning, patching and refresh become self-service requests within policy, instead of tickets waiting in the database team’s queue.
overview: A bank’s database team spends a surprising share of its week on the same three tasks: provisioning an instance, patching it, and producing a copy for a development team that has been waiting. Nutanix Database Service automates that lifecycle on infrastructure the bank already owns, so a copy becomes a self-service request within policy rather than a ticket in a queue. The measure that matters is provisioning and refresh lead time, and it is worth measuring carefully before automation, because afterwards nobody reliably remembers how long it used to take.

benefits.text: Provisioning and patching become automated operations rather than manual runbooks
benefits.limits: Automation covers the engines the platform supports; anything outside that list keeps its manual process and should be named

benefits.text: Development and test copies can be refreshed on request rather than scheduled weeks ahead
benefits.limits: Copies of production data into non-production carry the same data-protection obligations; masking is a separate control this does not provide

benefits.text: Database lifecycle runs on infrastructure the bank already owns and controls
benefits.limits: Sized from measured capacity and performance rather than from host counts or invoice history; a design built on the latter is a quotation with an architecture attached

residency: Databases and their copies remain on bank-owned infrastructure inside the bank’s data centres

notFor.situation: An estate whose databases are predominantly on managed cloud services
notFor.why: Those services already provide this lifecycle; duplicating it on-premises solves nothing

notFor.situation: A small database estate with stable provisioning demand
notFor.why: Automation overhead exceeds the manual effort it replaces at low volume

scope:
Model: Redington solutions engineering with an accredited Nutanix implementation partner · Duration: 8–12 weeks to a first engine set under automation with self-service enabled
Support model: Vendor support for the platform; Redington coordinates the vendor case.
1) Assessment — database inventory by engine, lead-time baseline, copy demand and data-protection position
2) Design — engine coverage, copy policy, self-service scope and capacity for copies
3) Build — automation deployed for the first engine set
4) Enable and hand over — self-service enabled within policy, operations handed over
deliverables: A provisioning request completes end to end without database-team intervention
A non-production copy carries the handling controls the copy policy requires
Engines outside the supported list are named explicitly rather than implied covered
effort: 8–12 weeks to a first engine set under automation with self-service enabled
languages: English delivery; Arabic operational documentation on request
